name: Kurt R. Oneto
title: Partner and Head of the Government Law Section, Nielsen Merksamer, Parrinello, Gross & Leoni LLP
background: Oneto holds a B.A. in Political Science, Phi Beta Kappa, from the University of California, Berkeley; an M.A. in Government from California State University, Sacramento, where his graduate research examined the effect of voter turnout on ballot measure outcomes; and a J.D. from the UCLA School of Law. Before joining Nielsen Merksamer, he worked for the California District Attorneys Association and completed internships with the California State Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives. (Source: Nielsen Merksamer LLP attorney biography.)

At Nielsen Merksamer, a Sacramento-based law firm specializing in California ballot-measure and initiative law, Oneto heads the firm's government law section and sits on its management committee. The firm's own profile describes him as a recognized expert in initiative and referendum law who has advised more than 60 statewide and local ballot-measure campaigns in California and six other states, with a practice covering California constitutional law, state budget procedure, tax law, and regulatory and administrative-enforcement matters. He has authored legal commentary on budget-related referendum procedure, including a Public Law Journal article on the City of Upland line of cases. (Source: Nielsen Merksamer LLP attorney biography.)

For the November 2026 California ballot, Oneto is the filer of record and initiative proponent for three measures represented in this voter guide: Proposition 41 (audits of special-tax programs and a bar on excluding new state taxes from the constitutional spending limit) and Proposition 42 (bars on new personal-property and retroactive state taxes), both filed with the Attorney General on December 8, 2025 and funded chiefly by Building a Better California, the committee whose largest identified donor is Google co-founder Sergey Brin; and Proposition 45 (the CEQA-streamlining 'Building an Affordable California Act'), filed October 21, 2025 on behalf of the California Chamber of Commerce, the measure's sponsor. Propositions 41 and 42 each carry a same-ballot conflict clause aimed at nullifying Proposition 40, the SEIU-UHW-sponsored wealth tax, if either outpolls it. (Source: content/measures/ca-prop-41-2026.json, ca-prop-42-2026.json, and ca-prop-45-2026.json in this voter guide, whose underlying sourcing includes Ballotpedia's pages for each measure and the California Secretary of State's qualified-ballot-measures listing.)

I could not independently verify a specific, named list of other ballot measures Oneto has personally filed or represented as proponent, beyond the 'more than 60 campaigns' figure his firm's own biography gives in general terms; Ballotpedia, which would ordinarily be the source for that kind of career-spanning list, was unreachable during this research (returning a 403 error even through a proxy), and this session's web search tool had exhausted its query budget before this profile was written. Because I cannot cite verifiable, specific prior measures with outcomes, past_measures_authored is left empty rather than populated with unverified examples.
